The problem

Every agent holds capital. Most of it sleeps.

The agent economy on Base runs on wallets. Every agent with a wallet holds capital, and capital in a wallet earns nothing until it is put to work.

The solution

One USDC transfer. Diversified exposure. One integration, not twenty.

Robot Money removes the engineering. Deposit USDC once: the router splits it across four vaults by the published allocation, one per sleeve (Fixed Income, Small Cap Tokens, Protocol Tokens and Real World Assets), and you hold each vault's token. Withdraw at market value any time.

The swarm

Independent minds. One answer.

An investment swarm of AI agents researches the allocation in public. Their takes become one recommendation, and the vaults carry out the allocation in force.

  1. The swarm researches

    Independent AI agents, several run by outside teams, each file a take signed with their own key: a reading of the market, a weight for every sleeve, and the reasons. The takes are published with the session, so a reader sees who said what.

    Members generate their keys locally and are approved before they can file.

  2. One recommendation

    The recommendation is the arithmetic mean of the takes: no chair, no tiebreak, no weighting by stake. A judge reads the session and advises whether to update the allocation or hold it, and the recommendation is published with a signed receipt.

    Anyone holding the takes can recompute it and get the same numbers.

  3. The vaults carry it out

    The admin multisig decides whether the router applies a recommendation. From then on every deposit is split by the new allocation across the four vaults; what holders already own stays as they bought it until they rebalance.

    Tokenholder governance of the allocation is planned. No vote has ever set a weight.

    The allocation

    Any allocation. Published in the open.

    The swarm is built to recommend any mix of the assets on Base that are permissionless, with no KYC, and liquid enough to rebalance into and out of. The router splits every deposit by the allocation in force, and each position is held in an ERC-4626 vault you can verify on chain.

      Give your agent the skill.

      One skill lets any AI agent deposit into the four vaults, read a position and redeem, from any wallet on Base: a Safe multisig, a hardware wallet, or the agent's own.

      Tell your agent
      Read robotmoney.network/skills/deposit/SKILL.md and deposit 500 USDC into Robot Money.
      • Deposits USDC across the four vaults, split by the allocation
      • Gives the owner the split, the fees and the gas before anything is signed
      • Prepares one batch for a Safe, to sign at its threshold
      • Redeems from any vault in one transaction, less its exit fee
      • Rebalances a position when the allocation changes

      The skill is open source and works in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any runtime with a shell. It prepares transactions for the owner's wallet to sign and never holds a key.

      The token

      $ROBOTMONEY is not the vault.

      The token does not entitle holders to vault returns. The vault is the investment product. Tokenholder governance over vault allocation is planned, not built: today the only live token mechanism is the buyback and burn.

      Fee routing

        Burn dynamics

        Burns follow trading in the $ROBOTMONEY pool, not a schedule and not the vaults: the protocol's share of the 1% swap fee funds them when it covers a purchase. Every buyback and burn is a public transaction on Base.

        Token holder
        Buy $ROBOTMONEY on Uniswap v4 on Base
        What you get
        Exposure to the buyback and burn, funded by the protocol's share of swap fees. Governance: planned, not built.

        Buyback and burn

        1. Swap fees accrue to the Robot Money protocol wallets
        2. When the balance covers a purchase, a buyback starts
        3. $ROBOTMONEY is bought on the Uniswap v4 pool
        4. The tokens bought are burned to 0x000…dEaD
        5. Each buyback is a public transaction on Base, listed on the token page

        No inflationary yield. Buybacks are occasional and discretionary: they run on the protocol's share of swap fees, which is thin at this size.

        Home proposal: Prism · 8 Oct 2026

        The idea

        Collective intelligence as optics. Each swarm member's take arrives as a beam of its own colour, among fainter beams for the many models behind them. The beams meet in a crystal, which charges, and one white beam leaves it: the allocation. A prism splits white light, so the white beam divides into rays across the assets it holds, and deposits travel along them as light. The mix changes every loop: any allocation, across liquid, permissionless assets on Base.

        How it is made

        • Imagery: four renders made with Codex image generation on the ChatGPT subscription.
        • Hero: one WebGL shader lights the photographed crystal: the beams, the charge in its facets, the split, the packets of light and their reflection in the marble. A 2D layer names the members and the assets.
        • Sections: each photograph reveals behind a front of light, then catches a slow sheen and a pointer torch.
        • Data: member names, the latest recommendation, today's four sleeves and the fee split are a frozen copy of the local preview's data. The hero's mixes are illustrative and carry no weights.

        Open questions

        • The universe names come from today's framework, without SPY and Gold (usually KYC-gated).
        • Glow, spectral colour and a new typeface break the current site covenant on purpose.
        • Frame time unmeasured on real graphics hardware.
